# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
Two landed in the ledger as docs/mistakes/M21 and M22. The rest are here.

THE ONE WORTH CARRYING ABOVE ALL OTHERS. Attacking your own work is what
produced every real result tonight. The passport producer passed its own
14-test suite and looked done. An independent strongest-tier reviewer, run in
a different context from the builder, returned NOT SOUND with a Critical that
was real: the tool answered "who did this work" from ACTIVE records only,
which on the live store silently dropped 183 records, while field 4 reported
nothing missing. The suite could not catch it because the suite was written by
the same session that wrote the code, and two of its tests passed for the
wrong reason. The decorrelation rule (W14 on the plan: the planner is not the
final verifier) earned its place the day it was written down.

A REGRESSION TEST THAT HAS NOT BEEN FALSIFIED IS NOT A REGRESSION TEST. After
fixing the Critical, the new test was proven by copying the tool outside the
repository, deleting the fix from the COPY, and watching the test fail with
the wrong session's name in its output. Evidence at
`~/Documents/BrotherModeUp-handovers/2026-08-15-seam-evidence/`. The repository
was never modified to run it.

A NUMBER TRUE IN ONE DIRECTORY IS NOT TRUE GENERALLY, and it landed three
times in four hours across two products, twice against sessions actively
looking for it. The seam figure, a chain node called unshipped from one root
scan, and an ignore rule verified in the one directory where it held. The form
that survives a tired session: a measurement is quoted with its tree and its
revision beside it, or it is not quoted.

TWO SESSIONS SHARING $TMPDIR SHARE THEIR GATE LOG. A concurrent session and
this one both wrote $TMPDIR/gate.log. The resulting file contradicted itself
inside one page, saying "2 SUITE(S) FAILED" while listing one. Only the
per-run --artifacts directory was trustworthy. Use a session-unique log path
and always pass --artifacts; the predecessor omitted it and lost the failure
text for two suites.

A CONTROL THAT CANNOT REACH A VERDICT IS NOT A PASSING CONTROL, and this
appeared twice tonight in two different products. BrotherMode's
check_install_identity SKIPs forever because the documented install writes no
stamp. BrotherSBE's design artifacts check returned NO-DATA forever because
one intake carried no tier key. Both were invisible until something made them
speak, and in both cases the first thing they said was true.

THE PROGRESS PAGE WAS INVISIBLE TO THE CONTROL THAT POLICES IT. bm_progress_check
globbed docs/plan/*GANTT*.html while the published board, linked from
PROJECT.md as the stable artifact, was NORTH-STAR-PUSH-BOARD.html. It reported
OWED (stale) against a file three days older. Widened, with a control test
proving a stale board is still reported stale.

CROSS-SESSION COORDINATION PAID FOR ITSELF, TWICE. The concurrent BrotherMode
session held the answer to a blocker this session was about to re-derive, and
released sole writer rather than colliding. The BrotherSBE session corrected a
number this session had already told the founder, verified three of its claims
read-only before accepting any, and handed over the exact assertion buried in
a log full of ResourceWarning noise. Neither exchange was ceremony; both
changed what was done next.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
